newsitem.title: FRANCE: Franc fall to 3.75 per DM could save EMU-economist.
newsitem.headline: Franc fall to 3.75 per DM could save EMU-economist.

text.p: A Geneva-based economics teacher, in a column in French afternoon daily Le Monde published on Tuesday, said the French franc should be allowed to fall to 3.75 francs per mark to boost growth.

Charles Wyplosz, economics teacher at the respected postgraduate Institute des Hautes Etudes, said such a fall would save European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), which would otherwise be hit by a wave of public anger at slow growth and high unemployment.

Dealers said talk of the article in Le Monde, one of a series from outside contributors which the newspaper is running, had briefly hit the franc, which dipped earlier to a low of 3.4251 per mark compared to 3.4207 this morning.
Wyplosz said that the government had no other policy tools to boost growth, given restraints on public spending contained in the Maastricht treaty.
"A fall of around 10 percent, with the mark at 3.75 francs, would have a clear and quick effect..." he wrote.

This would still allow the franc to remain within the fluctuation bands of the European Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM), widened in 1993 to allow currencies to move 15 percent either side of a central rate.

He suggested the Bank of France could manage a fall in the franc to 3.75 per mark without losing credibility, while maintaining the status quo would give the impression the central bank was locking itself into an indefensible position.

A 10 percent devaluation immediately would also tell markets that there would be no other change in the level of the franc between now and the end of 1998 when currency parities are due to be fixed ahead of the launch of the single currency in 1999.

The Bank of France has repeatedly said it aims to maintain the stability of the franc against the other main European currencies and in the past has raised interest rates if the French currency appeared at risk of falling sharply.
